newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan mid-sized life insurers' problem loans fall.
newsitem.headline: Japan mid-sized life insurers' problem loans fall.

text.p: Problem loans at Japan's medium-sized life insurance companies fell in the year to March 31, 1997 from a year earlier, according to data released by the companies on Tuesday.
Outstanding problem loans as of March 31, 1997 were as follows (in billions of yen, with year-ago comparisons):

The figures comprise loans to bankrupt firms, loans with interest payments in arrears by six months or more, loans on which interest rates have been cut to help cooperate restructuring, and loans to troubled clients.

The full names of the life insurers are Taiyo Mutual Life Insurance Co, Kyoei Life Insurance Co Ltd, Daido Life Insurance Co, Daihyaku Mutual Life Insurance Co, Toho Mutual Life Insurance Co, Nippon Dantai Life Insurance Co Ltd, Fukoku Mutual Life Insurance Co, and Tokyo Mutual Life Insurance Co. All of the life insurers are unlisted.
